label: Dry Creek Junction, symptom 'drive_grease_degradation'
headline: Dry Creek Junction's 8.8x tracker-drive grease signal is an aging 2017 block being greased reactively and coded as corrective work — 8 drives, 27.6 labor hours, no lost generation — fix it with a PM route addition, not a warranty claim.
action: Add the remaining 2017-vintage tracker drives at Dry Creek Junction to the existing tracker-drive lubrication PM route (as WO-2025-00537 recommends) and have the CMMS owner confirm these lube events are booked as PM rather than CM so the site's corrective rate stops reading as an 8.8x outlier.
reasoning: The eight members are eight distinct tracker drives (TR-B07-R055, TR-B01-R002, TR-B03-R059, TR-Z07, TR-B02-R019, TR-Z08, TR-Z12, TR-Z09) all receiving grease service or drive swaps on what the on-site tech explicitly identifies as a 2017-vintage block coming due together (WO-2025-00537), with no same-asset repeats, no P1s, no recorded lost MWh, and 27.6 total labor hours across 24 months — the signature of an orderly age cohort, not a defect. H2 (PM lapse) is weakened because Dry Creek does run tracker-drive lubrication PMs: control WO-2026-00150 is a PM regrease at this very site, and the comparator PMs at Kernwood Basin (WO-2024-00229), Coralito Flats (WO-2026-00162) and Ryegate Plains (WO-2026-00685) show the same physical work booked as routine_service elsewhere, which means much of the 8.77x lift is a CM-vs-PM coding channel rather than a hardware difference. H3 is real but not discriminating: the boilerplate narratives and incoherent resolution codes seen in members (CLEANED with parts_used=gearbox in WO-2024-00073; NO-FAULT-FOUND on part-replaced records WO-2025-00537, WO-2026-00574) are equally present in the controls (verbatim-duplicate warranty text in WO-2025-00023 and WO-2025-00595; PM regrease coded RESET in WO-2026-00150), so metadata noise is a fleet-wide corpus property, not something manufactured at Dry Creek. H4 is unsupported — environment is 'none_mentioned' on all eight members and no other seal- or dust-linked symptom is elevated in the controls. Net: a genuine but low-severity wear-out cohort whose apparent excess is amplified by classification, worth an O&M scheduling change and not a commercial claim.
contradicting: Three of eight events escalated past a regrease to gearbox replacement with scored gear faces (WO-2024-00073, WO-2024-00353, WO-2025-00874, plus WO-2026-00574 extracted as part_replaced), which is run-to-failure rather than clean wear-out and carries more cost than a scheduled lube; one member is coded Warranty (WO-2024-00353) despite a 2017 vintage, and a further CM grease event (WO-2026-00574) occurred in June 2026 after the Feb 2026 PM regrease (WO-2026-00150), suggesting the PM cycle may not yet cover the whole block. Asset-namespace mixing (TR-Z07/Z08/Z09/Z12 versus TR-B0x-Rxxx) leaves open that some records duplicate the same physical row, which would make the cluster smaller still.

population_detail.description: Eight distinct tracker drives in the 2017-vintage blocks at Dry Creek Junction already serviced or replaced; the un-serviced remainder of that same block is implied by WO-2025-00537 but cannot be enumerated.
population_detail.basis: Count of distinct asset_ids across the 8 member work orders; no installed-base or commissioning table was supplied, so the full 2017 cohort size is not derivable.

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is an age-cohort effect: a single 2017-vintage tracker block at Dry Creek Junction has reached its drive-grease service life, so lubrication work that is expected end-of-life wear is arriving as a burst of corrective work orders rather than reflecting any defect.
predictions: The 8 member assets should concentrate in a small number of blocks (the TR-Z* and TR-B01/B02/B03 groups) rather than being spread uniformly across all blocks at the site.
Assets of the same install vintage at other sites should show an elevated drive_grease_degradation rate too, once rate is normalised by vintage rather than by site.
Severity markers should stay low: labor_hours per WO ~2-7 (observed mean 3.45), lost_mwh per WO under ~1, priorities mostly P2-P4, and no P1s.
Same-asset recurrence within 12 months of a regrease should be absent; recurrence flags should point to other assets in the block, not repeat visits to one asset.
Once the cohort is worked through, the rate should decay: fewer new asset_ids in later periods and a rising share of previously-serviced assets.
discriminating_evidence: Install-date or commissioning field for the member assets: a tight vintage band supports H1; a spread across vintages kills it.

Fleet-wide query of drive_grease_degradation rate per GW-month restricted to same-vintage assets — if Dry Creek's lift collapses toward 1.0 under that stratification, H1 is favoured over a site-specific defect.
Presence of scored gear faces / gearbox replacements (3 of 8) rather than pure regreases would suggest run-to-failure, not orderly wear-out, and argues toward H2.

hypotheses.statement: Dry Creek Junction lacks (or has lapsed on) a scheduled tracker-drive relubrication PM, so grease degradation that other sites absorb silently as PM work surfaces here as corrective work orders, inflating the site's CM symptom rate without any difference in underlying hardware condition.
predictions: Dry Creek should have near-zero PM-type work orders with component=tracker_drive and a lubrication action, while comparator sites with low CM rates should have many.
Member WOs should be overwhelmingly wo_type CM/Warranty (observed: 7 CM, 1 Warranty) with no preceding PM WO on the same asset_id in the prior 12-24 months.
Escalation signature: a meaningful fraction of events should reach gearbox replacement or gear-face scoring rather than stopping at regrease (observed: 3 of 8 mention scoring/replacement).
At least one narrative should explicitly recommend proactive scheduling (observed in WO-2025-00537), and no follow-up PM work orders should appear in the months after that recommendation.
Cost asymmetry: mean labor_hours per drive_grease WO at Dry Creek should exceed the fleet mean for the same symptom, because reactive repacks and replacements cost more than scheduled greasing.
discriminating_evidence: Count of PM work orders per GW-month for tracker_drive at Dry Creek vs the top 5 comparator sites — a deficit at Dry Creek separates H2 from H1 and H3.
Whether a PM schedule change or contract change date precedes the onset of the cluster (first member 2024-07-06); an inflection at that date supports H2.
If comparator sites show the same total tracker_drive touch rate but classified as PM, the 8.77x lift is a coding-channel effect (H2), not a physical difference.

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is largely a data artifact: boilerplate/copy-pasted narratives, a dominant single reporter (TECH-0229 on 5 of 8), internally inconsistent resolution codes, and a very small exposure denominator (3.8 GW-months) combine to manufacture an 8.77x lift from what may be as few as 3-4 distinct physical events.
predictions: Verbatim or near-verbatim narrative strings should repeat across distinct wo_ids (the sentence 'The old grease had hardened right up and the gear faces were scored where it had been running dry. Row back in service and tracking with the block.' appears in WO-2024-00073, WO-2024-00353 and near-identically in WO-2025-00874/WO-2026-00574; 'That is the third one in this block this quarter. Normal wear for the vintage on these.' appears in WO-2024-00306 and WO-2025-00535).

Resolution_code should disagree with the extracted action at a much higher rate here than fleet-wide (observed: CLEANED with parts_used='gearbox'; RESET and NO-FAULT-FOUND on records extracted as part_replaced).

Asset_id namespaces should be inconsistent at this site (TR-B07-R055 style vs TR-Z07 style), suggesting two ingest paths or an unresolved asset master, with possible duplicate representations of the same physical row.
Removing TECH-0229's work orders should drop n from 8 to 3 and pull the rate per GW-month below roughly 0.8, i.e. lift under ~3.5.
Three separate WOs each claiming to be 'the third one in this block this quarter' should be mutually inconsistent with the actual per-block, per-quarter counts derivable from the member list.
discriminating_evidence: Exact-match and fuzzy-match diff of narrative text across the 8 members; high duplication favours H3 over H1/H2.
Reporter-stratified rate: if every other Dry Creek tech's drive_grease rate is at fleet baseline and only TECH-0229 is elevated, the signal is a reporting/coding habit, not equipment.
Asset master reconciliation — if TR-Z07/Z08/Z09/Z12 map onto the same rows as TR-B0x-Rxxx entries, the event count is inflated.

Poisson check on the raw counts: with fleet rate 0.24/GW-month and 3.8 GW-months, expected ~0.9 events; confirm whether an 8-event observation is genuinely outside plausible variation or driven by duplicate records.

hypotheses.statement: Site-specific environment — high summer ambient temperature and dust/grit ingress past drive seals at Dry Creek Junction — is thermally degrading and contaminating drive grease faster than fleet baseline, making this a real but environmental rather than manufacturing problem.
predictions: Event dates should skew to the warm season (observed: Jun x3, Jul x2, Sep, Nov, Dec — a summer lean but not exclusive), and a month-of-year histogram should show a significant June-September peak versus a flat fleet profile.
Other seal/contamination-linked symptoms at the same site (bearing wear, slew-drive backlash, seal failure) should also be elevated above fleet rate, not just grease degradation.
Narratives should mention dust, grit, heat or contamination in the environment field for at least some members — observed value is 'none_mentioned' on all 8, which is evidence against.
Affected assets should be spatially biased toward perimeter rows or rows adjacent to unpaved access roads rather than distributed by vintage.
discriminating_evidence: Environment tag frequency across all Dry Creek work orders for any symptom: if dust/heat is never mentioned anywhere at this site, H4 is weak relative to H1/H2.
Whether affected assets group by physical location (block/row position) versus by install vintage — location clustering favours H4, vintage clustering favours H1.
Cross-site comparison of other dust-sensitive symptoms at Dry Creek; elevation confined to grease alone points away from a general environmental driver.

exposure_note: Priced at the cost model's inverter replacement rate. This population is not inverters, so treat the count as the reliable figure and this dollar value as indicative only.
